subject: ventures/world-clock-widget
professional: a mobile/web developer who ships a world-clock or travel-planning app and cares about time zones and DST (first check: offsets across DST transitions and half-hour zones), plus an astronomer-minded reviewer who would check sunrise/sunset against a second ephemeris, including high latitudes near the solstice

evidence.correctness: Ran `node --test '*.test.mjs'` in site/ (53 pass). Recomputed 15 (city, instant) cases independently: UTC offset and local HH:MM against Python zoneinfo, incl. DST edges (New York 2026-03-08 06:59/07:00Z, London 2026-10-25 00:59/01:00Z, Sydney 2026-10-04 15:59/16:00Z, Auckland 2026-09-27 13:59/14:00Z): all 15 exact. Sunrise/sunset/daylight against an independently written NOAA (Meeus) solar-position calculation in Python (not the Almanac algorithm): London 21 Jun 04:42/21:21 vs 04:43/21:21, Tokyo 04:25/19:00 exact, Los Angeles 21 Dec 06:54/16:47 exact, Sydney 21 Dec 05:40/20:05 exact, Mumbai 06:43/18:49 vs 06:42/18:49, New York 8 Mar 07:19/18:54 vs 07:18/18:55: all within 1 minute, matching the claimed accuracy. BUT Reykjavik (64.1N, outside the polar circle) is wrong for 13 days around the solstice: a 365-day sweep of cityClock found daylightMinutes <= 0 on 16-28 June (e.g. 21 Jun: sunrise 02:55, sunset 00:03 pulled back a day, daylight -171 min, rendered as '-3h -51m', and at 22:00 local isDaylight=false 'night' while the sun is up until ~00:04). Only Reykjavik fails across 40 cities x 73 dates (2,920 points). Swift SolarCalculator is a line-for-line twin so it presumably shares the flaw; not run (no Swift toolchain here).
evidence.completeness: Checked web surface (site/index.html): local time per city, sunrise, sunset, daylight length, waking-hours band, 'vs. you' offset, add/remove, sort, share link, localStorage, opt-out, two guide pages, usage counting: all present in code and covered by page.test.mjs/solar.test.mjs (53 pass). Not verifiable here: the iOS/iPad/Mac app and WidgetKit widget (Sources/WorldClockApp, WorldClockWidget; ~800 lines) have never been compiled (README itself says 'unverified'; `which swift` finds no toolchain). VENTURE.yaml marks ios 'blocked-on-owner' yet says 'the code is complete and tested'. Polar/never-sets state is handled in code but the Reykjavik long-day case is a hole. Hypotheses untested, stage 'prototype'.
evidence.verification: `node --test '*.test.mjs'` in ventures/world-clock-widget/site: 53 pass, 0 fail. Mutations on solar.mjs, each reverted with git checkout (git status clean): (1) OFFICIAL_ZENITH 90.83 -> 90.33 (shifts every sunrise/sunset by ~2-3 minutes): 53/53 still pass, NOT caught (reference-value tolerance too loose); (2) removing Math.round in utcOffsetMinutes: not caught (near-equivalent); (3) moving the working-hours/evening boundary 17 -> 18: caught, 1 test failed. The equinox test explicitly avoids Reykjavik, so the one known failing region is untested. Swift tests (4 files) could not be run here; README says CI runs them on Linux.
evidence.craft: Read site/solar.mjs, usage.mjs, index.html script, Package.swift, SolarCalculator.swift. Clean ES module, pure functions, cached Intl formatters, every storage/clipboard access in try/catch, HTML escaped, comments explain why, polar null handled, share-link ids whitelisted against the catalogue. Defects: solarEvent day-nudge tries +1 then -1 day and silently returns the raw candidate on failure, so a sunset that is legitimately after local midnight gets moved to the wrong day (the Reykjavik bug); formatDuration does not guard negatives; reachability clamps rather than rejects; the ~380-line solar.mjs is a hand-maintained duplicate of the Swift engine (acknowledged, with an id-parity test).
evidence.claims: Backed: 'no network request' (grep of index.html/usage.mjs: only localStorage, no fetch/XHR); 'runs in browser'; Almanac for Computers 1990 algorithm (solar.mjs steps match the published algorithm); DST via IANA db (Intl, verified against zoneinfo above); disclaimer/no-warranty footer present; usage counts local-only. Not backed: 'accurate to roughly a minute outside the polar circles' (index.html, README, solar.mjs header) is false for Reykjavik 16-28 June (see correctness); VENTURE.yaml 'code is complete and tested' for the iOS app, which has never been built; llms.txt page links still point at duncan-haywood.github.io rather than marisstella.app (stale host, redirects exist); site/sitemap.xml has example.invalid placeholder hosts (assumed rewritten by the Pages build, not checked).
evidence.fitness: Job walked through: a person coordinating with family/colleagues in 3-6 cities opens the page, sees default six cities, adds Mumbai, sees 'vs. you' as +5h30m style deltas and a waking-hours label, copies a share link. Works end to end in the tested code paths; half-hour zones correct; sort by time of day is useful. Limits a user would hit: fixed 40-city catalogue (no search), no meeting planner/overlap finder (the core job of a travel/remote-team clock), waking-hours band ignores weekends. The iPhone widget (the headline of the name) is not reachable by anyone today.
evidence.domain: Compared against the US Naval Observatory Almanac for Computers algorithm (standard, public-domain, adequate for a clock; independent NOAA calculation agrees within 1 min at mid latitudes) and IANA tz handling via Intl (matches zoneinfo exactly, incl. DST edges and 30-minute zones). Departures: city-centre coordinates and no elevation (disclosed); Almanac algorithm degrades at long days above ~60N (undisclosed beyond a test comment); no twilight (civil/nautical) values a travel planner or photographer might expect. A practitioner would sign it off for mid-latitude use with the stated limits.

defects.what: Reykjavik shows negative daylight ('-3h -51m') and 'night' while the sun is up for 13 days around the June solstice: sunset falls after local midnight and solarEvent's +/-1-day nudge relocates it to the previous local day, so sunset < sunrise. Contradicts the 'accurate to about a minute outside the polar circles' claim.
Tests tolerate a ~2-3 minute systematic sunrise/sunset error: changing OFFICIAL_ZENITH from 90.83 to 90.33 leaves all 53 tests passing.
Equinox 'sunrise before sunset for every city' test explicitly avoids the Reykjavik solstice case where the invariant fails, so the invariant is never checked where it breaks.
iOS app and widget (~800 lines Swift UI) never compiled or run; VENTURE.yaml says 'code is complete and tested' while README says 'unverified'.
llms.txt links use the retired duncan-haywood.github.io host instead of marisstella.app.
No meeting-overlap / best-time-to-call planner, the core job for multi-zone users; 40-city fixed catalogue without search.

verdict: The browser tool is a small, careful, well-commented piece of work whose time-zone conversions are exactly right (15/15 against zoneinfo incl. DST edges) and whose sunrise/sunset agree with an independent NOAA calculation within a minute at mid latitudes, so a user can mostly rely on it. It does not meet the bar: Reykjavik, which is outside the polar circle, gets negative daylight and a false 'night' for 13 days around the solstice, contradicting the page's own accuracy claim; the 53 tests stay green when the solar zenith is shifted by 30 arcminutes (a 2-3 minute error); and the iPhone/widget half of the product that gives the venture its name has never been compiled. Recommended small fix: in solarEvent, resolve the local day by choosing the candidate (shift of -1, 0 or +1 UTC days from raw) whose local date equals the requested date and which keeps sunset after sunrise, add a Reykjavik 21 June test asserting daylight about 21h, and tighten the sunrise reference tolerance to 2 minutes.
